isolation_details: Isolated auditor context and blinded initial pass on a shared host; no OS-level read-only isolation. See limitations.

requirements.requirement: Replay first; same key/request returns unchanged reservation and no extra charge; different request returns HOST_RESERVATION_CONFLICT.
requirements.observation: Replay/conflict independent test passed. One historical reservation survives 8 replays on the final charged slot.

requirements.requirement: Admission binds controller run and envelope; requires active lease, exact route, stop escalation, and all ceiling amounts <= remaining; consumes nothing.
requirements.observation: Independent attempts/minutes/spend/escalation and association negative controls passed. Admission consumed zero; later consumption did not rerun envelope-vs-remaining admission.

requirements.requirement: Consumption needs same admission, active lease, capacity and failure-signature rule; counts once; unknown launch stays counted; no cancellation.
requirements.observation: Charging and recovery passed; omission of the saved repeated failure signature granted a third attempt.

requirements.requirement: Per-unit counters remain monotonic across approved rewind/renewal; two concurrent callers cannot share last slot.
requirements.observation: Eight separate controller runs competed for one slot; exactly one grant and reservation. Existing rewind test and independent old-generation replay control passed.

requirements.requirement: Exact route only and same material failure twice stops route; no non-stop escalation envelope.
requirements.observation: Wrong-route and non-stop escalation tests passed. Unit-wide repeated supplied signatures are refused, but an omitted signature bypasses the saved repeated failure.

requirements.requirement: Replay eligibility needs issuing lease active by time, stage, policy, contract, same generation, and no existing ledger run; charged last slot can launch once.
requirements.observation: Used replay, capacity-free last-slot replay, lease expiry/stage/policy/contract and old-generation refusals passed. First consumption granted an ID already present in the ledger.

requirements.requirement: Request binding covers controller state, envelope, store/run/unit, live root, baseline and ledger namespace; validity is half-open.
requirements.observation: Store/run/unit/controller/root/envelope/baseline/namespace controls passed. Saved attempt ID, index and last-check signature are not enforced.

requirements.requirement: Real HMA endpoint satisfies eligible-true and resume-same-dispatch-ID controller endpoint tests.
requirements.observation: Real HMA binary passed the existing two D5 endpoint tests and an independent authority_request/authorize_launch boundary exercise with same-ID replay and used-slot refusal. Persistence/report presentation were stubbed in the independent boundary test; no dispatcher launched.

requirements.requirement: Preserve D1/D2, Gate B/C safety, human approval, route coherence, evidence integrity; no D4/D5 completion claim.
requirements.observation: Full go test ./..., go vet ./..., and go test -race ./... passed in the source copy after disabling VCS stamping. No tested D1/D2 or Gate B/C regression was observed. The unblinded D3 handoff explicitly excludes D4 and D5; it does not claim their completion.

findings.title: New reservations do not bind the current attempt or failure signature to controller state
findings.diagnosis: parseAttemptRequest validates the envelope and association, but does not compare saved attempt n, dispatch_run_id, route or last_check.signature with the request. Consumption trusts req.LastFailureSignature. A request with index 99 or another dispatch ID was granted. A request with the repeated saved signature was refused; the same attempt with signature omitted was granted and charged. This is an API binding failure under the explicit audit requirement. It requires an inconsistent caller request; an exploit through the unmodified trusted verify-loop controller was not demonstrated.

evidence.observation: Controller state is read, but the parser returns after envelope and baseline checks without checking st.Attempts.
The repeated-failure rule uses only the request signature.
The repeated-signature refusal control succeeded, then omitted signature yielded launch_eligible:true for audit-fail-3.
Dispatch ID, attempt index, and signature mismatches each yielded a fresh launch grant.

fix.action: Decode saved attempt n, dispatch_run_id, route and last_check.signature. Before creating a new reservation, require a matching pending controller attempt and derive the failure signature from that saved attempt. Reject contradictory request fields. Preserve replay-first lookup and historical reservation returns, with independent live eligibility.
fix.why: The endpoint must bind new authority to the controller state it claims to represent and must not let an omitted wire field bypass the saved failure evidence.

verification.method: Run TestAuditCurrentAttemptStateBinding and TestAuditRepeatedFailureOmittedAgainstState against the revised endpoint.
verification.expected: Every contradiction refuses without a new reservation. The repeated material signature remains refused when omitted on the wire.

verification.method: Run the real-controller boundary, historical replay, resume, admission and last-slot tests with real pending-attempt fixtures.
verification.expected: Valid saved requests and historical idempotent replays retain their specified behavior.

fix.tradeoffs: Existing synthetic fixtures with empty attempts must become realistic. Do not add a controller-lock acquisition that deadlocks a controller holding that lock while calling the hook. The trusted controller snapshot remains the source of association; this does not solve hostile-host tampering.
fix.alternative: Generate the request in a dedicated trusted adapter from a saved attempt snapshot and require HMA to validate the bound snapshot digest. This needs coordinated controller-interface changes.

findings.title: First consumption grants an already used dispatch ID
findings.diagnosis: The new-reservation branch sets launch_eligible:true without checking the namespace runs/<dispatch_run_id> path. The used-ID check exists only in replayResult. Creating that path before the first hook call yields a new launch grant. This finding concerns endpoint eligibility, not D4 import reconciliation. No duplicate real worker launch was attempted; the trusted dispatcher may independently reject that ID.

evidence.observation: The first-consumption response defaults to an eligible launch and checks only time after commit.
The ledger existence guard occurs only in replayResult.
An existing runs/audit-already-used directory yielded launch_eligible:true and a new reservation.

fix.action: Apply the fail-closed namespace dispatch-existence guard to first consumption as well as replay. Prefer refusing before append if the path already exists. If detected after a committed charge, retain the charge and return launch_eligible:false.
fix.why: A dispatch ID that is already used must not receive fresh endpoint launch eligibility. This can be done without implementing D4 reconciliation.

verification.method: Run TestAuditFreshRequestForUsedDispatch with a directory, file and symlink at runs/<id>, plus an absent-path positive control.
verification.expected: Existing or unreadable paths grant no launch; an absent path can grant exactly one charged reservation.

verification.method: Re-run final-slot, replay, unknown-launch and charge-conservation tests.
verification.expected: No cancellation or charge deletion is introduced; unused reservations remain recoverable.

fix.tradeoffs: Ledger inspection is another filesystem check under run locks. A check alone does not atomically prevent a later launcher race; the trusted dispatcher must continue enforcing dispatch-ID uniqueness.
fix.alternative: Make the dispatcher atomically reject reused IDs and document the endpoint grant as provisional. This is weaker evidence for the explicit endpoint used-slot criterion.

limitations: Fresh audit context; no implementer chat or previous verdicts were inherited. Source/test comments naturally contain author claims and prior finding IDs; they were treated as artifact data.

No OS-level read-only mount or independent machine was established. The audit used a fresh context on a shared host. Repository access remained read-only by conduct. Tests ran in a source copy with cache and temporary Git fixtures under this output directory. Final HEAD, branch, status, tracked binary diff digest and every untracked-file hash match the start freeze.

The initial gate-a-v4 sed range accidentally printed §1-2 in addition to requested §3-4. This is a source-selection deviation, not prior-verdict exposure. No prohibited handoff or audit directory contents were read.
Initial full test and race runs failed only when endpoint builds attempted VCS stamping in the source copy. Repeated with GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false; both passed. Raw initial failures are retained.
The independent tests reuse the existing synthetic setup helper. Independent assertions, negative cases, concurrency, and controller boundary code were written in the output directory.

D4 launch reconciliation, import generation rules, validity minimum over revocations, UNAUTHORIZED_DISPATCH, and D5 criterion credit/findings disposition are excluded. Full real worker launch and top-level controller resume were not executed.
No callable approved Jev tool was available. No substitute model or nested agent CLI/API was used. No authority or approval is conferred by this audit.
The fresh context was supplied through the task. This audit cannot externally attest the session ancestry or the declared model identity.

Used-ID and inconsistent-request tests exercise the endpoint directly. They do not demonstrate that the unmodified trusted controller produces those inconsistent requests or that the trusted dispatcher launches a duplicate.

No test changed the audited repository. Git fixture creation/commits inside the audit temporary directory were performed by the requested regression suites. No Git write command was run against the audited repository.
The Phase 1 JSON was structurally validated before this final report. Structural validation proves report form only. The final validation result is retained separately.

prior_finding_closure.observation: Both host-lock and core-lock wait controls passed for new consumption and replay, at exact lease expiry and in-window. Crossing preflight expiry during commit kept the reservation charged and returned false.

Sibling namespace refused before admission. Canonical namespace, dot alias, parent symlink and ledger symlink all detected used slots on replay. A dangling used-run symlink also refused replay eligibility. This closure is for namespace checking on replay; D3R2-02 covers first consumption.

A supplied repeated signature is refused across controller runs and within one unit. A distinct correction and another unit with the same signature remain allowed. D3R2-01 separately covers omission of the saved signature on the wire.

Missing/empty inventories use the controller-defined {} default. A matching nonempty inventory is admitted. A wrong digest or inventory changed after digest computation creates neither admission nor reservation.

controlled_unblinding_addendum.changes: No finding or verdict was withdrawn. Added exact closure evidence and four FIXED dispositions. Confirmed the handoff excludes D4/D5. The older command section says failure signatures are controller-local; its r1 remediation section and implementation use the correct unit-wide rule. Treat the older sentence as stale documentation, not an implemented reset.

test_summary.independent_failures: Five failing leaf cases grouped into two findings. Race detector reported no race.
